summary: A new analytics substrate (python -m nora.analytics) derives typed stays and rule-labelled home/work places from Nora's presence record, entirely deterministic and consumer-neutral.
details: Ships OFF by default ([analytics].enabled = false) — no behaviour changes for any existing deployment until an operator turns it on.

Emits typed facts only, never natural language — no Nora tool, no app route, and no ambient behaviour reads from it yet (those are separate, later specs tracked as github.com/mikeng-io/nora issues #6-#9).
Presence retention raised from 180 to 720 days (~490MB at current volume) so the derived history survives long enough to eventually train a forecaster (a later tier, not part of this change).
A rename in identity.toml (former_person_ids) is now correctly merged into one derived subject rather than silently splitting a person's history across two identities.

Neutrality is enforced at build time: an import-linter contract forbids nora.analytics and nora.domain.mobility from importing any consumer-facing package (agent, app, platform, tag, doctrine, ingest, engagement, skills).

A backfill path (backfill_batch_limit, read off a subject's lag with no mode flag) makes a full parameter-change re-derive take minutes rather than the ~12 hours the steady-state batch size alone would need.
limitations: stay_radius_m and stay_min_dwell_seconds are inherited defaults (120m/600s), not yet validated against enough live data to tune.

Home/work labelling is intentionally conservative: a location with ambiguous evidence resolves to unlabeled rather than a guess. One class of work-from-home pattern is proven — not just observed — to be indistinguishable from a genuinely ambiguous case using the current single-signal (night-share) formula; a distinct-night-day-count gate is a candidate fix, documented but not yet built.

The rollup's per-subject failure isolation and liveness gauge exist, but the daemon has not yet been run against live traffic — enabling it is a separate operator decision (deploy/docker-compose.yml carries the service, off by default).
